author: Josh Butler
description:
Australia’s trade minister, Don Farrell, says tariff regime is unjustified and inconsistent with free trade agreement with US

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Donald Trump has hit Australian exports with new trade tariffs, claiming the country is not doing enough to combat forced labour, but the Albanese government has demanded he remove them immediately.

The Unit
title: Donald Trump hits Australian exports to US with new higher trade tariff over claims of ‘forced labour’

author: Hayden Vernon
description:
IRGC claims base in south-west England was used by US to launch bombing missions, making it ‘legitimate target’

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

The government has said the UK is “ready to defend itself” after Iran’s military warned that any bases being used by the US were “legitimate targets”.

The UK has allowed the US to launch “defensive” operations from British bases hosting American planes since the start of its war on Iran but has refused to help in offensive operations.

Continue reading...
title: UK ‘ready to defend itself’ after Iranian threat over US bases

author: Nick Robins-Early and agencies
description:
Elon Musk’s EV company lost a quarter of its value after revealing weak profits and high spending on AI and robotics

Tesla’s stock fell about 13.5% on Thursday in one of the biggest single-day market losses in the company’s history.

Elon Musk’s automaker has struggled throughout the year, losing about 27% of its market value as huge capital expenditures and weaker-than-expected profits worry investors.
title: Tesla stock suffers double-digit drop on carmaker’s worst day in years

author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
description:
Burnham says ‘no one in government loses when power is shared’ as he revives Brown-era national economic council

  • It’s not just a No 10 in the north, it’s an engine for growth throughout the whole UK | Andy Burnham

Regional mayors are to be given a leading role in the UK’s economic policy, Andy Burnham has said, as he called the opening of No 10 North “the biggest rebalancing of power our country has seen”.

The new prime minister has revived the national economic council [NEC], first set up by Gordon Brown to put the government on a war footing during the 2008 financial crash, arguing that economic growth requires the same level of urgency, focus and collective action.

Continue reading...
title: Regional mayors to take key roles in UK policy decisions as part of No 10 North plans

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Republican Blake Miguez is weighing what district to run in after state redrew map following supreme court decision

A congressional candidate from Louisiana who was the subject of a police report accusing him of rape – which he denies – says he is hoping to again “earn” Donald Trump’s endorsement as he considers precisely where to run amid redistricting.

The candidate, Blake Miguez, is weighing running in one of two districts, neither of which he lives in but which he is allowed to run. He has been mulling that choice after the supreme court’s landmark decision in Callais v Louisiana prompted the state to swiftly redraw its US House districts – and after he had secured the president’s backing under the previous congressional map.

Continue reading...
title: Louisiana House candidate accused of rape says he hopes to again ‘earn’ Trump endorsement

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Treasurer points to other reforms after Labor members call for ‘fairer return’ from natural resources. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Thanks Martin Farrer for kicking off the day, it’s Kat Wong here to take you through today’s news.

Australia’s resilient labour market continues to be a bright spot in the nation’s economy, Australian Associated Press reports.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: Jim Chalmers says he has ‘other priorities’ than a gas tax; Anthony Albanese calls to congratulate Andy Burnham

author: Dharna Noor
description:
‘Ratepayer Protection Pledge’ president has touted is non-binding as people continue to struggle with rising bills

Donald Trump has announced that about 200 entities have signed on to his non-binding “Ratepayer Protection Pledge”, expanding a voluntary commitment which claims to ensure US consumers will not bear the cost of the AI datacenter build-out.

Trump delivered remarks on Thursday at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) headquarters, alongside Lee Zeldin, the agency’s administrator, and Chris Wright, the energy secretary. Other attenders included governors who signed on to the pledge, including Brian Kemp of Georgia, Mike DeWine of Ohio, Spencer Cox of Utah and Jeff Landry of Louisiana.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says nearly 200 firms have signed pledge to protect Americans from costs arising from datacenters

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Residents in Ladera Ranch in Orange county voice concerns after six children diagnosed with Ewing sarcoma

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Concerns are growing in southern California over a cluster of “exceptionally rare” cancer cases that has sickened multiple children in a suburban community.

Families living in the Orange county neighborhood of Ladera Ranch, home to about 26,000 people, have reported that six children in the community were diagnosed with Ewing sarcoma, Katrina Foley, the vice-chair of the county board of supervi
title: Southern California suburb alarmed as ‘exceptionally rare’ cancer sickens multiple children

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Conservative leader is becoming more confident and forging a message for her party, but faces a new opponent

“So, Andy Burnham seems like a nice guy.” Those were the slightly unexpected opening words of Kemi Badenoch’s first speech since the change in prime minister. But make no mistake: she was there to bury her opponent.

Even Badenoch-sceptics inside the Conservative party and farther afield agree the Tory leader is becoming more confident, and has been able to forge an increasingly coherent message for her party, one based on a promise of economic competence.

Continue reading...
title: Kemi Badenoch ‘has to adapt’ her rhetoric to take on Andy Burnham

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Agent came under suspicion after allegedly providing info in MS Now report about vice-president’s helicopter trip

A Secret Service agent assigned to JD Vance’s protective detail is “the subject of an administrative investigation, and potential criminal inquiry, involving allegations of compromising operational and information security”, according to the Secret Service chief of communications.

The agent came under suspicion after allegedly providing information that appeared in an MS Now report about the vice-president’s planned Marine Corps helicopter trip with his son to a golf lesson, a source told CNN.
title: Secret Service agent on Vance’s detail under investigation

author: Associated Press
description:
Vance Boelter receives two life terms after admitting politically motivated killings and shootings

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The Minnesota man who pleaded guilty to killing a top Democratic lawmaker and her husband was sentenced to spend the rest of his life in prison on Thursday, a little over a year after the political attacks.

Vance Boelter, 59, was sentenced to two consecutive life terms plus 40 years in prison after pleading guilty in June to the six counts related to the killings of the former house speaker Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark, and the shootings of state senator John
title: Minnesota man sentenced to life for killing Democratic lawmaker Melissa Hortman

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
CEO Chris O’Shea defends Centrica’s plans as it reports rise in retail profits as it focuses on bigger margins

The owner of British Gas has claimed that most households would rather speak with an AI chatbot than deal with the company’s staff as it prepares to cut 1,300 jobs from its call centres.

Centrica, the supplier’s FTSE 100 owner, plans to cut 800 jobs as the company carries out a “targeted deployment of AI tools”, on top of the 500 cutsit confirmed last month.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Customers prefer AI chatbots,’ says British Gas owner as 1,300 call centre jobs axed

author: Maya Yang
description:
No injuries or deaths were reported from early-morning temblor whose epicenter was 68 miles from Amarillo

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A 5.0-magnitude earthquake struck the Texas panhandle, the state’s northernmost region, on Thursday, marking the strongest quake to hit the area since 1900.

The earthquake struck at around 5.21am at a depth of 3.5 miles (5.7km), according to the US Geological Survey (USGS). Its epicenter was about 27.8 miles south-east of the city of Spearman and approximately 68 miles from Amarillo.
title: 5.0-magnitude earthquake strikes Texas panhandle

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
Strategy will tackle ‘public health disaster’ that claims more lives than fire, flooding or knife crime

A national strategy to address the “public health disaster” of drowning has been launched in England – hours after two women died at an Essex beach, the latest in a surge of water-related tragedies.

Among the measures being considered are: providing every child in England with water safety education and swimming lessons; establishing how climate change can increase risks; and media campaigns to inform bystanders how to respond to a potential drowning.

Continue reading...
title: Mission to ‘eradicate scourge of drowning’ after deaths surge across England

author: Anna Betts
description:
Forecasters warn of US coastal flooding, heavy rain and dangerous surf as the storm tracks west

Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall in Louisiana on Wednesday afternoon, and is moving westward toward the Texas coast, where it is expected to reach later on Thursday, bringing rainfall, winds and rising water levels.

In a Thursday morning update, the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said that Bertha was moving west and that the center of the tropical storm was expected to move near or along the Louisiana and upper Texas coasts over the next several hours before moving inland over Texas on Thursday evening.

Contin
title: Tropical Storm Bertha heads for Texas after Louisiana landfall

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Resolution, which comes after similar one in June, is largely symbolic, as Trump administration says it’s unconstitutional

  • US politics live – latest updates

The US House of Representatives on Thursday for the second time passed a war powers resolution directing Donald Trump to withdraw the US military from the conflict with Iran, amid renewed fighting in the Middle East that has driven oil prices to their highest levels in weeks.

The resolution proposed by Democrat Pramila Jayapal passed by a 214-208 vote, with four Republicans joining all Democrats in attendance to vote in favor.
title: US House passes war powers resolution directing Trump to withdraw US military from Iran

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Committee accused of trying to ‘weaponize’ justice system via ‘laughably weak and vindictive criminal referral’

Democrats have accused the US House of Representatives judiciary committee of a “baseless” and “vindictive” attack on former special prosecutor Jack Smith after it referred him for criminal prosecution for allegedly lying to Congress over his investigation into Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election.

Committee chair Jim Jordan, an Ohio Republican, wrote to acting US attorney general Todd Blan
title: Republican-controlled committee refers former Trump prosecutor Jack Smith for criminal investigation

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Officials ‘do not know’ how to respond to potential changes to plans to start freeing up to 6,000 offenders

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham’s pledge to review early release plans has created “a sense of chaos” across the Prison Service, probation officers have said.

As Whitehall insiders confirmed the prime minister was examining possible exemptions to the law under which offenders will be freed, the Napo probation union said prison officials “do not know” how to respond.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham’s review of prison early release scheme is causing chaos, says union

author: Timothy Pratt
description:
Concern over US effort to prosecute Sam Tunick, accused by authorities of wiping his phone using GrapheneOS

The US Department of Justice is attempting to prosecute an Atlanta resident in connection with the movement against the police training center known as Cop City because he had GrapheneOS on his phone, an open-source operating system that enables users to enter a passcode and wipe a phone clean.

The case, which had its first hearing on Monday, centers on a little-known US federal statute that makes it a crime to destroy property in an effort to prevent it from being seized.

Continue reading...
title: US government targets Cop City protester over phone operating system

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Law change means renters and flat owners may be able to cut bills as energy costs soar amid Iran war

British households will be able to buy plug-in solar panels later this summer after the government changed the law so the UK’s biggest retailers could bring them to market for the first time.

People across the country will be able to join the millions across Europe generating their own electricity using “balcony solar panels” from 27 August, according to legislation passed last week.

Continue reading...
title: UK households free to install plug-in balcony solar panels from end of August

author: Martin Belam
description:
Conflict continues across the region as White House announces nuclear technology agreement. Plus, the artist who flattened a Tesla with a tank

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. The US has signed a landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could allow the kingdom to enrich uranium in the future. The deal will be submitted to Congress for review, where it could face opposition among lawmakers who fear a lack of monitoring safeguards.

In lengthy talks stretching over more than one administration, the US has feared that Riyadh would look elsewhere for nuclear technology if the US did not provide what it wanted. Saudi Arabia has long said that if it does not partner with the US, it coul
title: First Thing: US agrees Saudi uranium deal as strikes on Iran continue and Yemen’s Houthis hit tankers

author: Associated Press
description:
Woolsey died of a stroke at Washington home after facing ‘Havana syndrome’ reported by some government officials

R James Woolsey, a national security expert who led the CIA for two turbulent years after his appointment by Bill Clinton, has died. He was 84.

Woolsey, who became CIA director in early 1993, died on Tuesday at his home in Washington, according to several newspapers. Conchita Sarnoff Woolsey, his wife, told the newspapers that he died from a stroke.

Continue reading...
title: R James Woolsey, embattled ex-CIA director under Bill Clinton, dies aged 84

author: Vivian Ho
description:
Donald Trump’s decision to attack Iran without first seeking congressional approval has sparked further controversy over the National Defense Authorization Act

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

In addition to passing the National Defense Authorization Act – a key plank of the president’s plan to spend $1.5tn on the military in the 2027 fiscal year – House Republicans on Wednesday agreed to begin the process of writing a $95bn bill to fund the war with Iran.

The passage of this budget resolution paves t
title: Outcry after $1.15tn defense bill passes in the House – US politics live

author: Associated Press
description:
Shah will face Republican Jay Freely, a Trump-backed former NFL kicker, in November for battleground seat

Amish Shah won the Democratic primary on Wednesday in a hotly contested congressional district in Arizona, delivering another defeat to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, which backed a rival, as more voters reject the preferences of party leaders in Washington.

Shah, an emergency physician, will face Republican Jay Feely, a former NFL kicker who was endorsed by Donald Trump in his primary, in the fall. Before becoming political opponents, Feely and Shah were part of the same team — the New York Jets. Shah was a doctor on the sidelines, while Feely was the kicker.
title: Amish Shah wins in Arizona Democratic House primary in blow to establishment

author: Natasha May
description:
Family and friends of residents eligible for dining and hotel packages as city spurned by visitors

  • Middle East crisis – live updates

Dubai is offering to pay family and friends of residents to visit in an effort to revive tourist numbers that have plummeted since the city was drawn into the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Dubai Invite scheme, an initiative of the department of economy and tourism, allows residents of the United Arab Emirates to nominate friends and relatives to receive benefits worth more than 3,000 UAE dirham (about £610) for their visit.

Continue reading...
title: Dubai offers tourists benefits worth £610 as numbers plummet amid Iran war

author: Sam Levine in New York
description:
Republicans have latched on to the announcement after Trump’s lie-laden speech, but experts say DHS’s data is ‘designed to create a false argument’

Donald Trump and his allies quickly seized on an announcement from Mikie Sherrill, the New Jersey governor, on Tuesday that 6,600 noncitizens had registered to vote because of a software error, and fewer than 400 of them voted, using thedisclosure to escalate false claims that there are scores of noncitizens on the voter rolls.

Trump seized on the news days after he said in a primetime speech<
title: Why New Jersey’s erroneous noncitizen enrollment is far from proof of election fraud

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Exclusive: Ro Khanna says ‘reindustrialization’ effort would provide grants, loans and investments to smaller businesses

Democrats in the US Congress have laid out plans for what they say would be the “boldest” bid to revitalize the country’s industrial heartlands since the second world war – using revenue raised by tariffs on China.

A bill introduced this week would create a new bank to strengthen domestic manufacturing, provided with up to $15bn in funds each year.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic lawmakers propose bank funded by China tariffs to boost US manufacturing

author: Anna Betts
description:
Angel Rampersad, Michael Swinton, Isabella Gonzales and Tyler Feehan were among 18 US troops killed in the war

A 30-year-old husband and father of two. A 25-year-old officer just weeks away from earning his MBA. A 19-year-old recent high school graduate. And a 28-year-old from Queens, New York, with a “radiant smile”.

The Pentagon this week identified three American service members who were killed, and a fourth believed to have been killed, in the Middle East over the past week amid an escalation in attacks between the United States and Iranian forces.

Continue reading...
title: The latest US troops killed in Trump’s Iran war are remembered for lives of service

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
The prime minister said the £100m package would mean the typical pub would save around £1,100 in the next financial year

Iain Hoskins, owner of Ma Pub Group in Liverpool, said that an extra 20% relief on business rates would go some way to “chipping away” at the rising cost but cast doubt on how many venues would be covered by the change.

He told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme:

The worry has been, obviously, in recent years, I mean, when our venues from last year to this current year got revalued, we saw increases of between 100% and 150% on the rates that we pay.

So that just goes to show how much they went up by. And while 20% – particularly if that 20% is on top of the 15% and other help that’s there – that can be very meaningful for businesses, independent businesses such as mine; I don’t want to sound ungrateful, but the increases were so huge last year that now we’re sort of chipping away at some of those increases.

We’re not actu
title: Burnham offers 20% cut in business rates for pubs, clubs and live music in England – UK politics live

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Budget airline, which has two US investment firms vying to buy it, also affected by passengers booking later

The low-cost airline easyJet has revealed a 70% slide in profits because of soaring fuel costs and later bookings as a result of the conflict in Iran, only weeks after it agreed to a £5.7bn takeover.

The carrier reported a pre-tax profit of £85m between April and June compared with £286m during the same period a year earlier, as its fuel costs increased by £105m after the outbreak of hostilities in the Middle East in late February sent energy prices rocketing.

Continue reading...
title: EasyJet profits plunge 70% as fuel costs soar amid Iran war

author: Dan Jervis-Bardy Chief political correspondent
description:
Criticism comes as prime minister frames unity as point of difference to political opponents, saying ALP chooses ‘progress over protest’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Outspoken Labor MP Ed Husic claims the party has become “allergic” to dissent and dispute, warning the unity on show at its tightly controlled national conference could backfire.

The former industry minister broke ranks with the government on the first day of Labor’s 50th party conference to support a gas export tax, endorse Indigenous truth-telling and press for more criticism of Israel’s conduct in Gaza.

Conti
title: Husic says Labor ‘allergic to dissent’ as he breaks ranks on key government positions at party conference

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Hackers access Australian customers’ names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and some bank account details, company says

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Origin Energy customers’ addresses, phone numbers and partial bank account data have been accessed in a hack, the company has confirmed.

The firm has 4.8m customer accounts in Australia, providing electricity, fossil gas, LPG and internet services to homes and businesses.
title: Personal and banking details among customer data stolen in Origin Energy hack

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
CBA chair says contempt charge over closing speech by Rajiv Menon KC has left lawyers fearful of doing their job

The prosecution of a leading human rights barrister for contempt of court over his closing speech during a trial of Palestine Action activists has left lawyers fearful of doing their job, the chair of the Criminal Bar Association (CBA) has said.

Rajiv Menon KC is due to stand trial next week, accused of breaching the judge’s directions in the trial of six people for a 2024 direct action protest at an arms factory of the Israeli subsidiary Elbit Systems UK in Filton, near Bristol.

Continue reading...
title: Palestine Action trial lawyer’s prosecution criticised as ‘chilling’ for profession

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
NT minister for trade and business Robyn Cahill makes scientifically inaccurate claims while pushing to make territory ‘datacentre capital of the globe’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Northern Territory minister has been criticised for scientifically inaccurate claims that groundwater in the Northern Territory needs to be used to prevent the Earth’s magnetic poles from flipping.

The NT minister for trade and business, Robyn Cahill, made the claim while speaking in Darwin last week about the government’s push to make the territory “the datacentre capital of the globe”.
title: Politician’s claim Earth’s magnetic poles could flip if NT doesn’t use more groundwater criticised by experts

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Live, rolling coverage of business, economics and financial markets as government says it will review reliefs for ‘anti-social’ businesses

A bit more from the Night Times Industries Association lobby group, which is also wary of the small print – while welcoming the broad policy.

Michael Kill, its chief executive, said he wanted to know in particular which live music venues would be excluded. He said:

We are still awaiting the full details and eligibility criteria, which are expected to be announced at the autumn Budget. We will also seek clarity on the proposed exclusion of the largest live-music venues and continue to press for the final scheme to provide the broadest possible support.

The government is undoubtedly making the right noises. We look forward to continuing this constructive dialogue and ensuring these commitments translate into tangible and inclusive support for businesses throughout the night-time economy.
title: Andy Burnham to cut tax for pubs, clubs and live music in England and make vape shops pay more – business live

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
One Nation leader labels family violence leave ‘ridiculous’ and decries ‘woke’ support of women’s rights in November podcast

Pauline Hanson has described paid leave for those experiencing family and domestic violence as “ridiculous”, and suggested the issue is taking police away from “real crime”, calling for the family law system to be “wound back”.

In an unearthed interview, the One Nation leader said the advancements of women’s rights in the family law system over the decades had become “broken” because they favoured women and were now “suppressing the males all the time”.

Continue reading...
title: Pauline Hanson says domestic violence prevents police from dealing with ‘real crime’ in unearthed interview

author: Roque Planas and agency
description:
Shooting happened on street in popular neighborhood lined with restaurants, bars, shops and homes

A police officer in Madison, Wisconsin, shot and killed a man Wednesday in an incident that was captured on cellphone footage, sparking local protests.

John Patterson, the Madison police chief, acknowledged the shooting at a news conference, but stressed footage circulating was just one perspective of what happened.

Continue reading...
title: Police officer fatally shoots man in Madison, Wisconsin, sparking protests
